worked_solution:
For a function $f:{R}^{n}\to R,$ given by

$$
f:{{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}⟶f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}),
$$

the second derivative of $f$ is given by the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{″}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{1}∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}^{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{2}∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}_{n}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

The Hessian determinant $H(x,y)$ is the determinant of the second derivative:

$$
H(x)=det({f}^{″}(x))
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{″}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

First, notice that since
${f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x) & \operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}],$
we must have

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x),\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y).
$$

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x))=-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y))=\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x))=\operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\, & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)+y\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y))=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}
$$

So, the second derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(x,y) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{x}^{2}} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂x∂y} \\ \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂y∂x} & \frac{{∂}^{2}f}{∂{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(y-x)+y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y) & 2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-y)-y\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-y)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Evaluating the second derivative at $(\pi ,\pi ),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{″}(\pi ,\pi )=[\begin{aligned}-\pi  & \pi  \\ \pi  & -\pi \end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
H(\pi ,\pi )=(-\pi )\cdot (-\pi )-\pi \cdot \pi =0.
$$

For a function f:Rn→R, given by f:[x1x2⋮xn]⏟x⟶f(x1,x2,…,xn), the second derivative of f is given by the n×n matrix f″(x)=[∂2f∂x12∂2f∂x1∂x2⋯∂2f∂x1∂xn∂2f∂x2∂x1∂2f∂x22⋯∂2f∂x2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂2f∂xn∂x1∂2f∂xn∂x2⋯∂2f∂xn2].

The Hessian determinant H(x,y) is the determinant of the second derivative: H(x)=det(f″(x))

In our case, we have f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2].

First, notice that since f′(x,y)=[ysin⁡(y−x)cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y)], we must have ∂f∂x=ysin⁡(y−x),∂f∂y=cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y).

Now, we compute the second partial derivatives: ∂2f∂x2=∂∂x(ysin⁡(y−x))=−ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂x∂y=∂∂x(cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y))=sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂y∂x=∂∂y(ysin⁡(y−x))=sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)∂2f∂y2=∂∂y(cos⁡(x−y)+ysin⁡(x−y))=2sin⁡(x−y)−ycos⁡(x−y)

So, the second derivative is f″(x,y)=[∂2f∂x2∂2f∂x∂y∂2f∂y∂x∂2f∂y2]=[−ycos⁡(x−y)sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)sin⁡(y−x)+ycos⁡(x−y)2sin⁡(x−y)−ycos⁡(x−y)].

Evaluating the second derivative at (π,π), we obtain f″(π,π)=[−πππ−π].

Finally, we have H(π,π)=(−π)⋅(−π)−π⋅π=0.
